evidence:
This is a standard Fourier computation, and the single-neuron version is already in print. I read both PDFs with pdftotext.

(1) Morwani et al., ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2311.07568), App. F.1 Eq. (5):
- They define eta~_{u,v,w}(delta) := E_{a,b}[u(a)v(b)w(a+b-delta)].
- They derive eta~(delta) = p^{-3} sum_j uhat(j) vhat(j) what(-j) rho^{j delta}, noting "(only terms where j+l = k+l = 0 survive)".
- Eq. (6) and what follows give the class-weighted margin 2/((p-1)p^2) sum_{j != 0} uhat vhat what(-j). This becomes 4/((p-1)p^2) sum |uhat||vhat||what| cos(theta_u+theta_v-theta_w), which is our cosine/phase form.
- The Theorem 7 proof outline repeats the identity.

(2) Li, Liang, Shi, Song, Zhou, AISTATS 2025 (arXiv 2402.09469), Def. D.5 and Lemma D.7 proof:
- For k inputs, eta~(delta) = E[w(a1+...+ak-delta) prod u_i(a_i)] = p^{-(k+1)} sum_j what(-j) rho^{j delta} prod_i uhat_i(j). This is exactly our product-neuron beta_ij for general n.
- Lemma F.1 and Thm G.1 use the network-level diagonal mode: the max-margin f has fhat(j1,j2,j3,j4) > 0 when j1=j2=j3=-j4 != 0.

(3) Nanda et al., ICLR 2023 (2301.05217) and Gromov 2023 (2301.02679): the learned or analytic circuits compute cos(w(a+b-c)). I confirmed this from the abstract pages only. Neither states the averaging lemma.

(4) In general harmonic analysis, averaging over the coset c = sum a_t - delta keeps only the Fourier coefficients on the annihilator (Poisson summation on finite abelian groups). This is textbook material; I did not fetch a specific source.

What is new: stating the identity for an arbitrary network table (off-diagonal part = interference; the same identity applies to ReLU), and pairing j with -j to get Re(beta_j) cov_j(delta). Both are trivial extensions.

Search: I fetched the Morwani PDF, the Li et al. PDF, and the Nanda and Gromov arXiv abstract pages. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/r2-spectrum/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Supports eq:spectrum and app:spectrum. App. F.1 Eq. (5) proves eta~_{u,v,w}(delta) = p^{-3} sum_j uhat(j)vhat(j)what(-j) rho^{j delta}, the n=2 single-neuron case, together with the cosine/phase form in Eq. (6).

Supports the n-operand product-neuron form of beta_ij. Lemma D.7 (proof) gives eta~(delta) = p^{-(k+1)} sum_j what(-j) rho^{j delta} prod_i uhat_i(j). Lemma F.1 and Thm G.1 single out the network-level diagonal mode fhat(j,...,j,-j).

recommended_change: After eq:spectrum in approach.tex, add: "This is the network-level form of the single-neuron identity of \citet[App.~F.1, Eq.~(5)]{morwani2024feature} and \citet[Lemma~D.7]{li2025nsum}." In app:spectrum, open with "The computation is that of \citet[App.~F.1]{morwani2024feature}, applied to a general logit table." Optionally, use one notation for the product-neuron factor throughout: approach.tex writes conj(what(j)) and appendix.tex writes what(-j), which are equal for real w.
